To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the log-log form is not the best one, (2) the log-linear form is not the second best one, (3) economies of scale and densities exist, (4) the estimated economies of scale are smaller than previously found by Guldmann, (5) the estimated densities are smaller than previously estimated by Guldmann and larger than previously estimated by Pindyck, (6) the economies of scale and the densities are not as strong as previously estimated by Gulld

(1) the estimated cost functions are log-linear; (2) the estimated scale economies are constant; (3) the estimated density elasticities are positive; (4) the density elasticities are larger for larger systems; and (5) the estimated density elasticity for a large system is larger for larger systems.

(1) gas distribution costs increase with market size, and (2) the elasticity of gas distribution costs with respect to density is less than one, i.e. there exist economies of scale and economies of density. (author's abstract)
In summary, our research is concerned with
the estimation of gas distribution costs.
the specification of the cost function for the urban gas distribution sector.
the estimation of the relationship between gas costs and density and market size variables in urban areas.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for the gas distribution industry, there is a strong case for the log-linear functional form.
the log-linear form is not necessarily the best choice for estimating the relationship of interest.
there is no single best specification of the relationship between distribution costs and density.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the functional forms of the distribution cost equations should be carefully selected, and that a simple log-linear form may lead to misleading conclusions.
, although the log-linear forms seem to be a good approximation, the Box-Cox form is preferred.
the log-linear forms previously selected are not necessarily the most appropriate ones.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the functional form of the cost function is important and should be selected with care.
the functional form of the relationship between distribution costs and market variables is not a trivial issue and should be carefully examined before drawing any policy conclusions.
the functional form of the cost function is crucial for the estimation of scale economies and density effects.
